mcqs.question: During Kashmir's shrinking-snowfall episode, what were the February precipitation figures and deficit reported?
options: 14.2 mm against a normal of 130.4 mm, an approximately 89% deficit
100.6 mm against a normal of 284.9 mm, a 65% deficit
5.3 mm against a normal of 130.4 mm, an approximately 89% deficit
14.2 mm against a normal of 284.9 mm, a 65% deficit
mcqs.explanation: February precipitation was 14.2 mm, compared with the normal 130.4 mm, representing an approximately 89% deficit. The 100.6 mm and 284.9 mm figures refer to winter precipitation from December to February, not February alone.

mcqs.question: Which combination correctly describes the reported February conditions in Srinagar during Kashmir's unusually warm and dry winter?
options: 5.3 mm precipitation and an approximately 15.6°C February temperature, with the temperature described as a record
14.2 mm precipitation and an approximately 15.6°C February temperature, with the temperature described as a record
5.3 mm precipitation and an approximately 5.3°C February temperature, with the temperature described as a record
100.6 mm precipitation and an approximately 15.6°C February temperature, with the temperature described as a record
mcqs.explanation: Srinagar recorded 5.3 mm of precipitation, among the lowest since 1901, while its February temperature was approximately 15.6°C, described as a record. The 14.2 mm figure is Kashmir's February precipitation, whereas 100.6 mm is the December–February winter total.
